items.headline: Indian cargo vessel struck off Oman on Nov 2 — one sailor killed, 13 rescued; a distinct Gulf shipping attack, newly surfaced to the watch

items.headline: Iran nearly doubles its Hormuz blacklist — 114 vessels added Nov 2, spanning Sinokor, KOTC, Bahri and ADNOC-linked ships
bullets: Seatrade Maritime News (Nov 2): Iran's PGSA added 114 vessels to its non-compliance list on Nov 2 — the largest update since the list began in August — and confirmed Sinokor's entire fleet will be treated like listed ships. At least 29 of the additions are Sinokor-linked, 10 KOTC, 7 Bahri and 6 ADNOC; the list now holds at least 46 Sinokor-linked vessels, about half that fleet.

This is the executed action the watch was waiting on for Sinokor: it moves from the Oct 27 fleet-wide warning to actual listings, and widens the pressure beyond Sinokor to Gulf state carriers — even as the Doha draft sits with Washington and oil settled Monday sharply lower on diplomacy hopes ($104.77/$96.46). No detention or attack on a newly listed vessel has been reported.
